chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said: O people,
Fear Allah, Who is such that when you speak He hears, and when you conceal (a secret) He knows it,
And hasten to meet death, which will overtake you even if you run away from it, catch you even if you stay, and remember you even if you forget it.

key_terms.أَدْرَكَكُمْ: Overtake you / Catch up with you
key_terms.أَضْمَرْتُمْ: You concealed / You kept secret in the heart

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali say about the inevitability of death and Allah's knowledge?
ai.summary: In this eloquent address from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) links divine omniscience with the inevitability of death, urging believers to actively prepare for the latter rather than passively awaiting it. This exhortation reflects the Shia emphasis on *mawt* (death) not merely as an end, but as a transition requiring conscious readiness (*istidraak*) through righteous deeds. The rhetorical structure highlights that death pursues humanity whether they flee from it, remain stationary, or neglect its reality, underscoring the urgency of spiritual vigilance.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 203. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said: O people,
fear Allāh Who is such that when you speak He hears and when you conceal (a secret) He knows it.
Prepare yourself to meet death which will overtake you even if you run away, catch you even if you stay and remember you even if you forget it.
